source.title: MoE Sparsity Begets Monosemanticity: Insights into Understanding and Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Ming-Xue Tian; Qi Zhang; Xiao-Han Wang; Jia-Jun Chai; Guo-Jun Yin; Wei Lin; Cai-Lian Chen; Qi-Min Xu; Si-Yu Wang; Yi-Sen Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures expert-level monosemanticity in MoE models, not SAE feature splitting or the other specified SAE claims. Its MoE sparsity result is a related finding, not a test of the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study varies MoE expert-activation sparsity and measures layer-wise decoupling scores (LDS). It does not train SAEs of different dictionary sizes, match or partition SAE features, test absorption or canonical units, or compare SAE objectives. The MoE sparsity result is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study scores the monosemanticity of MoE experts as top-k expert activation sparsity varies. It trains no SAEs and varies no dictionary size. It does not track coarse features splitting into finer ones, feature families, absorption, canonical units, or SAE objectives. SAEs serve only as an analogy, so none of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that MoE sparsity promotes expert-level monosemanticity, that middle layers are the most specialized, and that experts are either domain-specific or general. Their EDMRS expert-selection fine-tuning matches or beats full fine-tuning in-domain and improves out-of-domain retention.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes MoE expert activations and LDS; it does not conduct SAE dictionary-size or feature-splitting experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported LDS trend varies with MoE activation sparsity; the study also reports LDS profiles across layers.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, lowering expert-activation sparsity (raising k) reduces the layer-wise decoupling score in four layers, with values shown only in Figure 3a.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher top-k expert-activation sparsity in MoE LLMs goes with higher expert-level monosemanticity, as scored by LLM explanations.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.10 is a case study comparing semantic granularity: an expert's explanation is more abstract than those of its constituent neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoE experts encode coarser concepts than their internal neurons.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The MoE sparsity result is indirect for the SAE claim. Figure 3a is the reported source for its values, while the text does not state the tested sparsity or k values or numeric LDS results.

untested.parts: All parts: SAE dictionary-size scaling, coarse features replaced by finer ones, coverage of inputs, directional proximity.
All parts: splitting in large models and in open SAE releases.
All parts: nested, geometrically close feature families mirroring a concept hierarchy.
All parts: absorption of parent latents by child latents, and the effect of SAE size or sparsity on it.
All parts: larger-SAE latents decomposing into smaller-SAE latents, novel latents, and the absence of canonical units.
All parts: splitting as an artifact of the SAE objective, and Matryoshka or other objectives.

record.verdict_notes: This is an MoE interpretability and fine-tuning paper. It is unrelated to SAE feature splitting apart from motivation by SAE sparsity. None of the claim's original sources is involved.

versions.untested_parts: SAE dictionary-size scaling, feature replacement, input partitioning, and directional proximity.
Splitting in large models or open SAE releases.
Nested SAE feature families, geometric closeness, and correspondence to a concept hierarchy.
Parent-child SAE firing overlap and whether SAE size or sparsity changes absorption.
Combinations of larger- and smaller-SAE latents, novel latents, and completeness or atomicity across dictionary sizes.
Whether SAE training objectives cause splitting on correlated or hierarchical inputs, and whether Matryoshka SAEs change it.

rows.subject: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507
rows.operation_detail: Measured LDS while varying MoE expert-activation sparsity by changing the number of activated experts.
rows.measure: Layer-wise Decoupling Score (LDS), the average EMS of experts in a layer
rows.value: figure only; text states that reducing sparsity consistently and substantially decreases LDS across all evaluated layers and k values
rows.note: The stated direction is that greater MoE activation sparsity corresponds to stronger expert-level monosemanticity. The result concerns MoE experts, not SAE feature splitting.
rows.check: The row measures expert-level monosemanticity (LDS) in an MoE as activation sparsity varies. That is not SAE feature splitting, so it bears on no version. It is better kept as a fits_no_version finding. The k values and the LDS numbers are given only in Figure 3a.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
